narrative.overview: Riprap reads like a public-works survey sheet brought to a desk: cool paper, navy ink, drafting labels in a highway-signage mono, and a federal blue that marks what can be checked. Depth comes from tonal layering of paper surfaces and hairline rules, not shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper surfaces in three tones, navy text, one federal-blue accent.
Sofia Sans for reading; Overpass Mono for data, labels and citation marks.
Evidence tier carried by a square's fill, hue as reinforcement only.

rules.name: The Checkable Blue Rule
rules.body: Federal Blue means a source or a control you can act on. Do not use it for decoration or headings.

rules.name: The Signal Budget Rule
rules.body: Amber and red appear only for hazard signal (warnings, alerts, severity). A calm briefing has none.

rules.name: The Twelve Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Text a reader must read is at least 12px.

rules.name: The No-Elevation Rule
rules.body: No box shadows on report content.

dos: Do keep every numeric claim next to its citation mark.
Do carry evidence tier and severity by shape as well as colour.
Do make an omitted section read as intentional, not broken.
donts: Don't add or swap a typeface, recolour the dam mark, or introduce a hue family.
Don't rename the Five Stones; add plain-language subtitles instead.
Don't use shadows or rounded card chrome on report content.
